what_it_does: Graph Neural Networks that operate on graphs changing over time — for example, a social network where friendships are added and removed — must combine two very different styles of computation: one that spreads information across the graph's connections (the graph learning part), and one that tracks how each node changes over time (the sequence memory part, similar to a recurrent neural network). Spreading this work across multiple chips is hard because the time-ordering of events creates strict dependencies: you can't process event B until you've finished event A. DiTile-DGNN identifies which events in a large batch are genuinely independent from one another so they can safely run in parallel, while also detecting when two nodes' internal states are similar enough that one can stand in for the other, allowing the dependency chain to be safely broken. A flexible hardware design ties the chips together with a communication network that can reconfigure itself to match whichever computation style is needed at each stage.
